title: Sun to Earth: flares, CMEs and storms
idea: Light from a flare arrives in 8 minutes. Charged particles take hours to days, and they shake Earth's magnetic field.

rows: Sudden disturbance: low frequencies hit hardest

compare.how: A flare's X-rays thicken the D layer on the daylit side. Lower frequencies fade first.
A temporary disturbance in Earth's magnetic field from arriving particles.
A storm's one bonus: it can reflect VHF signals.

traps.why: That's particle speed. A flare's X-rays travel at light speed: 8 minutes.
That's the flare's light. A CME is a cloud of particles: 15 hours to several days.

traps.wrong: It enhances propagation on all HF frequencies
traps.why: It disrupts, and the lower frequencies more than the higher.
A storm degrades the paths over the poles.

traps.wrong: The position of the Moon in its orbit
traps.why: It's the Sun turning on its axis: about 27 days.
Charged particles from coronal holes disturb HF.
